name: Mardi Himal Trek
sub_region: Kaski District, Gandaki Province (Annapurna Conservation Area)

difficulty.notes: Ridge trek; summit-day from High Camp (3,580 m) to Upper Viewpoint (4,200 m) or Base Camp (~4,500 m) is the hardest day, with exposed, windy ridge and a long descent. Forest Camp to High Camp is a ~1,000 m sleeping-altitude gain if done in one day. [s4][s5]

duration_days.notes: 5-day route is standard (40-45 km); 3-day version descends all the way to Siding on the summit day; 6-8 day versions add nights at Low Camp/Badal Danda. Many trekkers turn at the Upper Viewpoint (4,200 m) rather than Mardi Himal Base Camp (~4,500 m). [s4][s5]

max_altitude_point: Mardi Himal Base Camp (Upper Viewpoint at 4,200 m is the common turnaround)

itinerary.route: Pokhara - Kande (drive) - Australian Camp (2,060 m) - Pitam Deurali

itinerary.notes: Forest Camp listed ~2,500-2,600 m. Dense rhododendron/oak forest, few views. [s4][s6]

itinerary.route: Forest Camp - Low Camp - Badal Danda - High Camp
itinerary.notes: Low Camp ~2,985 m; Badal Danda ~3,210 m. Sleeping at Low Camp/Badal Danda is a safer option. [s4][s5]

itinerary.route: High Camp - Upper Viewpoint (4,200 m) - Mardi Himal Base Camp (~4,500 m, optional) - descend to Low Camp/Badal Danda
itinerary.notes: Pre-dawn start; MBC is ~1.5 h beyond the Upper Viewpoint. [s5]

itinerary.route: Low Camp - Siding - drive to Pokhara

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP)
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per foreign national (SAARC NPR 1,000), tax included

guide_requirements: Mardi Himal Trek is explicitly listed by NTB as a route requiring a licensed guide via a registered agency since 31 March 2023. [s3]

logistics.notes: Basic teahouses at Forest Camp, Low Camp, Badal Danda and High Camp; High Camp rooms are basic with shared bathrooms. [s5]

highlights: Close views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) from Badal Danda and the ridge [s4][s5]
Sunrise over Annapurna South, Hiunchuli and Dhaulagiri from the Upper Viewpoint [s5]
risks: Large sleeping-altitude gain Forest Camp-High Camp (~1,000 m) [s4]
Exposed, windy ridge; afternoon wind and cloud [s5]
Long knee-heavy descent on the summit day [s5]

acclimatization.notes: No rest day in the standard 5-day plan; splitting at Low Camp or Badal Danda is advised for slower trekkers. [s4]

unverified: TIMS requirement in practice (NTB lists it; operator reports say only ACAP is checked in Annapurna).
Exact Mardi Himal Base Camp altitude (~4,500 m) and Siding altitude (~1,700-1,750 m) vary slightly between operator sources.
